/* Animações */
@keyframes fadeSlideUp {
  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(24px); }

.reveal-ready {

  transform: translateY(38px);
  transition: opacity 0.72s ease, transform 0.72s cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1);
  transition-delay: var(--reveal-delay, 0ms);
  will-change: opacity, transform;
}

.reveal-ready.is-visible {

  transform: translateY(0);

```{=html}
<section class="rc2-section" id="framework">
  <div class="rc2-section-title"><h2>Scientific coordination</h2></div>

  <div class="rc2-text">
    <p class="rc2-lead">
      Rede C2 articulates research groups, permanent plots and methodological
      references for the long-term study of vegetation dynamics in Brazil's
      seasonally dry ecosystems.
    </p>

    <p>
      The network brings together field sites in Caatinga and Cerrado, combining
      local ecological knowledge with shared monitoring principles. Its structure
      supports comparable observations of plant communities, including vegetation
      structure, floristic composition, recruitment, mortality, regeneration and
      environmental context.
    </p>

    <p>
      Scientific coordination within Rede C2 is organized around interoperability:
      field decisions, plot metadata, taxonomic information, functional traits and
      environmental layers are documented so that data produced by different teams
      can be interpreted jointly across regions and through time.
    </p>
  </div>
</section>
```

```{=html}
<section class="rc2-section" id="integration">
  <div class="rc2-section-title"><h2>Integration principles</h2></div>

  <div class="rc2-text">
    <p>
      The network is structured to support both local monitoring and broader
      ecological synthesis. Each participating group preserves the specificity of
      its field site while contributing to a shared analytical framework for dry
      forest and savanna systems.
    </p>

    <ul class="rc2-compact-list">
      <li><strong>Field continuity:</strong> permanent plots and repeated censuses provide the empirical basis for detecting changes in vegetation structure and composition.</li>
      <li><strong>Methodological compatibility:</strong> protocol references guide plot establishment, remeasurement, stem records, regeneration modules and complementary environmental observations.</li>
      <li><strong>Data harmonization:</strong> standardized tables and controlled vocabularies make it easier to combine plot metadata, species records, demographic events and environmental descriptors.</li>
      <li><strong>Ecological synthesis:</strong> comparable datasets support analyses of vegetation dynamics, resilience, restoration potential and spatial turnover across Caatinga and Cerrado sites.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</section>
```

```{=html}
<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {

  const revealTargets = document.querySelectorAll(
    ".rc2-section, .content-card, .rc2-page-hero, .team-controls, .team-card"
  );

  revealTargets.forEach((el, index) => {
    el.classList.add("reveal-ready");
    el.style.setProperty("--reveal-delay", `${Math.min(index, 8) * 45}ms`);
  });

  if (
    window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches ||
    !("IntersectionObserver" in window)
  ) {
    revealTargets.forEach(el => el.classList.add("is-visible"));
  } else {
    const revealObserver = new IntersectionObserver(entries => {
      entries.forEach(entry => {
        if (entry.isIntersecting) {
          entry.target.classList.add("is-visible");
          revealObserver.unobserve(entry.target);
        }
      });
    }, {
      threshold: 0.12,
      rootMargin: "0px 0px -8% 0px"
    });

    revealTargets.forEach(el => revealObserver.observe(el));
  }

  const sections = document.querySelectorAll("section[id]");
  const navLinks = document.querySelectorAll(".navbar a[href]");

  if (sections.length && "IntersectionObserver" in window) {
    const navObserver = new IntersectionObserver(entries => {
      entries.forEach(entry => {
        if (!entry.isIntersecting) return;

        const id = entry.target.id;

        navLinks.forEach(link => {
          const href = link.getAttribute("href") || "";
          link.classList.toggle("active-section", href.endsWith("#" + id));
        });
      });
    }, {
      rootMargin: "-35% 0px -55% 0px",
      threshold: 0
    });

    sections.forEach(section => navObserver.observe(section));
  }

});
</script>
```
